original_question: For parameters delta > 0, lambda > 0, and n in N_0, define F_n^{lambda,delta}(t) = integral from 0 to t of (t-theta)^delta C_n^lambda(cos theta) (sin theta)^(2 lambda) dtheta for 0 < t < pi, where C_n^lambda is the Gegenbauer polynomial. Is it true that F_n^{lambda,delta}(t) > 0 for all t in (0, pi] if and only if delta >= lambda + 1?
target_in_paper: Section 6, Conjecture 6.1 ('Positivity of an integral involving Gegenbauer polynomials'), explicitly noted there as a restatement of [5, Conjecture 1.4].
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's target statement almost verbatim: it has the right quantity F_n^{lambda,delta}(t), the correct parameter ranges delta>0, lambda>0, n in N_0, the strict positivity requirement for all t in (0,pi], and the exact threshold delta >= lambda + 1.
missing_details: Make N_0 explicit as {0,1,2,...} so the question is fully stand-alone.
Specify that lambda and delta are real parameters.

Clarify the endpoint convention at t = pi: the paper writes the definition for 0 < t < pi but then asks positivity on (0,pi], so a stand-alone formulation should say that the same integral formula is also used at t = pi.
If you want the formulation to be paper-faithful as a citation target, identify it as Conjecture 6.1 in Section 6, restated there from [5, Conjecture 1.4].
refined_question:
Let N_0 = {0,1,2,...}. For real parameters lambda > 0 and delta > 0, and for each n in N_0, define
F_n^{lambda,delta}(t) = integral from 0 to t of (t-theta)^delta C_n^lambda(cos theta) (sin theta)^(2 lambda) dtheta,
for 0 < t < pi, and at t = pi by the same integral formula, where C_n^lambda denotes the Gegenbauer polynomial. Is it true that, for every lambda > 0, delta > 0, and n in N_0, one has F_n^{lambda,delta}(t) > 0 for all t in (0,pi] if and only if delta >= lambda + 1?
justification: The draft clearly targets the open problem in Section 6, not the unrelated earlier sections of the report. The nearest official formulation is therefore Conjecture 6.1 itself, which the paper states in essentially the same words as your draft. I did not broaden the question to the surrounding positive-definiteness consequences on spheres, because in this paper those are only motivation and context, not the conjecture being posed. The only refinements needed were to make N_0 explicit, specify the parameters as real, and remove the small endpoint ambiguity between the displayed definition on 0 < t < pi and the subsequent positivity claim on (0,pi].
